title: Gadgets: Personal app vibe coding that is actually safe — Kenton Varda, Cloudflare
talk_summary: Kenton Varda demos 'Gadgets', a Cloudflare Workers-based platform where each user instantiates their own copy of a vibe-coded app, with sharing/access control enforced by the platform rather than app code. The security model runs untrusted generated UI in a null-origin sandboxed iframe and server code in a dynamic worker sandbox, so XSS or other app-level bugs can't leak data.

takeaways.what_they_do: Generated client code runs in a null-origin iframe with CSP, talking only via postMessage/RPC to generated server code in a dynamic worker sandbox; neither can reach the outside world, so app-level security bugs are contained.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there is no security bug you can have in this code that matters

takeaways.what_they_do: The whole platform runs locally on the laptop via the open-source workerd runtime, so demos and testing don't depend on network or remote infra.

takeaways.technique: Per-instance app copies instead of shared multi-tenant app
takeaways.what_they_do: Each gadget instance is a separate copy of the code+data for one use case, so customization and sharing are per-instance and the platform owns access control.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when I instantiate this app, it is only for one slide deck. If I want multiple slide decks, I make multiple instances
